summary: Named on an Alberta lookout list; public sources describe the 127-site network but nothing specific to this tower's history.

facts.agency: Wildfire staff with Alberta Agriculture and Forestry

evidence.supports: Enilda is named on the Alberta lookout list
Alberta map shows 127 wildfire lookout sites across the boreal forest and Rocky Mountains
evidence.quote: Map showing the locations of Alberta's 127 wildfire lookout sites, which are situated throughout the province's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: 127 wildfire lookout sites across the boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains
evidence.quote: One hundred and twenty-seven wildfire lookout sites are located throughout Alberta’s boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: boreal forest towers built on high hills to see over obstacles
evidence.quote: towers, built on high hills in the boreal forest, which elevated the observer over any obstacles to vision.

evidence.supports: lookouts are located where visibility is favourable for detecting and reporting wildfires
evidence.quote: Fire lookouts are an integral component of wildfire detection in Alberta and are located where visibility is favourable to detect and report wildfires.

evidence.supports: each site staffed by a lookout observer, watching all day, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: wildfire lookout sites are isolated; staff must prepare for a range of possibilities, including a curious bear
evidence.quote: Wildfire lookout sites are isolated and the staff that work them must be prepared for a wide range of possibilities, including an encounter with a curious bear.

evidence.supports: wildfire staff are with Agriculture and Forestry (facts.agency); they have adopted BearSmart recommendations for many sites
evidence.quote: Wildfire staff with Agriculture and Forestry have adopted a number of Alberta BearSmart recommendations for many of their sites

sources.title: Alberta BearSmart and Alberta’s fire lookouts

corrections.current: Active fire lookout, staffed March–October; it is the observer's seasonal home. No public access to the tower or cabin — please don't visit uninvited.
corrections.proposed: Active fire lookout, staffed generally April to October; it is the observer's seasonal home. No public access to the tower or cabin — please don't visit uninvited.
corrections.why: Alberta's open data says sites are staffed generally from April to October. No public source read gives March. For human review.

notes_for_editor: PROTECTED DATA: the built year (2016), 30 m height, elevation, access mode and the record's March-to-October staffing note all come from the Alberta Wildfire WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT layer. Its metadata says the layer is classed Protected and should not be displayed on maps the general public will see. I kept those values out of the story and facts. Decide before publishing them. NO TOWER-SPECIFIC SOURCE: searches and reads found no public history of this lookout by name. The story is network-level context only. The 'operating lookout today' line was removed in the 2026-10-20 fact-check because no public source supports it for this site; consider holding it until a site source turns up. ACCESS: the record's 'closed' is not stated by any source, so facts.access is omitted; the story no longer says the site is operating today (removed in the 2026-10-20 fact-check). A 2017 geocache page for Enilda (GC71F2M) says the gate is closed in winter and the tower is manned through fire season. I did not use it as a source and it is not an invitation to visit. WIKIPEDIA: the Enilda article is about a hamlet in Big Lakes County and does not mention a lookout, so it is not cited. The 2009 Alberta lookout map text in the cache lists the name, but its public URL is not recorded, so it is not cited. No photos found.
